subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open-model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Costa <elena.costa@finserv.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned on pain, success metrics, and the immediate next steps. Please correct or add anything I missed.

Top pain points you called out
- Growing per-token costs with current OpenAI usage across chat + embeddings, especially at 10M+ monthly tokens.
- Vendor lock-in concerns: prompts, tool integrations, and function/tool calling behaviors that are tightly coupled to OpenAI/Anthropic APIs.
- Latency spikes for interactive products (target P95 <= 300ms for chat routes).
- Data residency & compliance needs for EU customers and internal auditability for regulated workflows.

Current stack we learned about
- OpenAI for chat + some embeddings (primary today).
- Anthropic used selectively for safety-critical summarization flows.
- Custom prompt templates + a small orchestration layer that assumes OpenAI-compatible request/response shapes.
- Kubernetes infra with a mixture of cloud-hosted GPUs for batch jobs; embeddings are stored in a managed vector DB.

Success criteria for a migration pilot
- Achieve parity in response quality for key prompts (3 representative prompts we defined).
- Reduce per-unit inference cost by >= 30% in pilot workloads.
- Maintain or improve P95 latency for chat routes (<= 300ms target).
- Preserve function/tool-calling and streaming UX for your frontend.
- Pass your security/compliance checklist (SOC 2 evidence, audit logs, KMS integration).

Compatibility needs we should prioritize
- API compatibility for streams, function/tool calling, and structured outputs.
- Tokenizer and embedding spec compatibility (embedding dims and semantic similarity characteristics).
- Easy model switching/fallbacks and clear quality/cost tradeoffs.

Initial open-model shortlist we propose for evaluation
- Llama 3 family (8B / 70B) — strong instruction-following and ecosystem tools for quantization.
- Mistral-Instruct / Mistral 7B — cost-effective with good instruction performance.
- MPT-30B-Instruct — robust across longer-context tasks (worth validating for doc-heavy flows).
- Falcon-40B-Instruct — strong baseline for instruction tasks in some of our benchmarks.
(We’ll provide per-model expected footprint, latency/cost estimates, and prompt adapters for your 3 test prompts.)

Suggested next steps
1) We’ll share a proposed pilot scope and timeline (attached: redwood_migration_plan.pdf).
2) Please send over the security questionnaire you mentioned — we’ll coordinate with our security team to get SOC 2 artifacts and the required evidence.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineering team next week to walk through integration points and benchmarking harness.
4) Agree on the 3 prompts and evaluation criteria so we can run apples-to-apples comparisons.

If that sounds right, I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep-dive and the pilot doc. Thanks again — looking forward to partnering on this migration.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Rishi — this is a great summary and captures everything we discussed. A few quick clarifications and asks: 

- Cost target: 30% reduction is attractive — can you include both steady-state and peak-cost estimates in the pilot doc? We have bursty usage in sutured hours.
- Latency: the 300ms P95 is for the user-facing chat product; for internal summarize pipelines we can tolerate higher latency.
- Tokenizer/embeddings: we need the embeddings to be compatible with our current vector index (same or compatible dims and distance metrics).

Attached is our security questionnaire (FinServ_Security_Questionnaire.pdf) — please have your security/compliance contact fill out or provide the referenced artifacts (SOC 2 report, encryption/KMS details, data retention policies).

We’re open to the shortlist — would like to prioritize models that require minimal prompt surgery and support streaming/function calling. A pilot next week works for our infra folks; Tue or Wed morning PT are best.

Elena
Sr. Product Manager, AI
FinServ Inc.
elena.costa@finserv.com
